project.name: @wickedevolutions/mcp-obsidian
project.description: External MCP server for safe multi-vault Obsidian operations across 75 filesystem tools, 1 explicit app-contact tool, and 28 Obsidian CLI tools (104 current-main tools total), with exact/approximate graph provenance and optional local semantic retrieval.

nodes.name: analytics.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Exercises vault analytics handlers for orphan notes, broken links, stale notes, health, and duplicate-basename backlink resolution.

nodes.name: cli-tools.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests CLI-tier tool definitions and mocked or live Obsidian command, Base, sync, template, and customization operations.

nodes.name: config.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests single- and multi-vault configuration resolution, containment checks, and symlink race protection.

nodes.name: cross-vault-graph.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests declared cross-vault graph normalization, eligibility, bounded metadata, and identity-preserving edge aggregation.

nodes.name: crossvault.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests cross-vault search, note lookup, URI inventory, ecosystem statistics, semantic search, and graph annotations.

nodes.name: discover-tools.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests discover_tools pagination, tool metadata, categories, and inventory consistency.

nodes.name: eval-baseline.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Defines Ollama-gated baseline evaluation tests for retrieval quality measurements.

nodes.name: fallback-reason-surfaces.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests that graph-provider fallback reasons remain explicit across graph analysis and cross-vault signal surfaces.

nodes.name: files.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests core vault file handlers, including read, create, update, delete, metadata, search, move, and round trips.

nodes.name: fs-promoted-a.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests promoted filesystem tools for daily notes, tasks, tags, properties, outlines, counts, and aliases.

nodes.name: fs-promoted-b.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests promoted filesystem tools for mutation, discovery, workspace, Bases, plugins, snippets, and themes.

nodes.name: get-started.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests dynamic and static guidance returned by the get_started tool, including truthful tier and linking guidance.

nodes.name: graph-fallback-reason.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests graph construction fallback reporting and sanitization when the Obsidian provider fails.

nodes.name: graph-link-counts.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests unresolved-link normalization and graph link-count aggregation under mocked provider behavior.

nodes.name: graph-provider-contract.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests that graph-provider output preserves the expected resolved-link and edge contract.

nodes.name: graph.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests graph extraction, ranking, levels, cancellation, handler output, and cached graph signals.

nodes.name: handler-smoke.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Runs non-error smoke checks across the assembled handler surface.

nodes.name: helpers.mjs
nodes.summary: Provides temporary vault creation and cleanup helpers shared by the test suites.

nodes.name: markdown.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests Markdown parsing, safe file creation, frontmatter updates, and path traversal rejection.

nodes.name: provider-state-matrix.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests graph provider states, fallback semantics, cache recovery, and surfaced capability metadata.

nodes.name: reranker-hyde.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests reranker registration, passage retrieval, semantic reranking, and HyDE behavior with Ollama-gated coverage.

nodes.name: resolver-hints.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests edit-distance hints and structured missing-vault or missing-note responses across handlers.

nodes.name: safety-bytedelta.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests byte-delta reporting for file and section mutations against on-disk sizes.

nodes.name: safety-readonly.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests read-only mode refusal of vault mutators while retaining readers and derived-index tools.

nodes.name: safety-untrusted.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests opt-in untrusted-content wrapping for reader outputs without changing errors or mutators.

nodes.name: sections-query.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests section append, prepend, update, and note-query handlers against structured Markdown notes.

nodes.name: semantic.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests embedding index accounting plus Ollama-gated semantic search, similarity, and indexing handlers.

nodes.name: tool-surface.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Verifies the tool registry, handler parity, built snapshots, dynamic vault schemas, and disabled-tool filtering.

nodes.name: transport-smoke.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Smoke-tests stdio and HTTP transports for authentication, cancellation, large requests, and clean shutdown.

nodes.name: wikilink.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests wikilink parsing, resolution, indexing, and link-navigation handler behavior.

layers.name: Safety & Transport
layers.description: MCP process bootstrap and HTTP transport expose the tool registry while central vault configuration enforces explicit targeting and filesystem safety boundaries.

layers.name: MCP Tool Surface
layers.description: MCP tool definitions, schemas, discovery, and handlers provide the filesystem, vault, graph, cross-vault, analytics, and Obsidian-facing operations.

layers.name: Graph & Provider Architecture
layers.description: Graph construction, provider state, parsing, traversal, ranking, digesting, and cross-vault normalization distinguish exact Obsidian capabilities from filesystem approximations.

layers.name: Retrieval & Evaluation
layers.description: Optional Ollama-backed embeddings, hybrid reranking, local storage, watching, and retrieval metrics implement and measure semantic note retrieval.

layers.name: Core Vault Foundations
layers.description: Shared vault-targeting, markdown and URI parsing, resolver hints, and common types support safe note resolution across filesystem and runtime tiers.

layers.name: Obsidian CLI Bridge
layers.description: The runtime-only bridge invokes the Obsidian CLI for capabilities that are unavailable through the filesystem provider when Obsidian is closed.

layers.name: Test Architecture
layers.description: Node test-runner suites, live-test support, fixtures, and contract coverage verify transport, safety, provider honesty, graph behavior, retrieval, and MCP tool surfaces.

layers.name: AI Team & Development
layers.description: AI-team operating guidance, development templates, prompt content, and the Codex worker adapter define the repository's collaborative development workflow.

layers.name: Build, Release & CI Infrastructure
layers.description: Package metadata, runtime configuration, packaging verification, CI workflows, and issue intake automation build, test, and distribute the external MCP server.

layers.name: Documentation & Architecture Artifacts
layers.description: User-facing and release documentation, live and reranker guidance, contribution and security policies, and tracked architecture visualization metadata describe and support the project without being runtime product code.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start here for the external Obsidian MCP server's purpose, installation choices, and operating limits. The README introduces the explicit named-vault model and frames the rest of this tour around truthful capability boundaries rather than assumptions about a running app.

tour.title: Server Transports
tour.description: The main entry point loads configuration, creates the MCP server, registers its tools and prompts, and attaches the standard-input/output transport. The optional HTTP server follows the same server contract for request/response deployment, so transport selection does not redefine product behavior.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript modules keep transport setup separate from the shared server instance, making alternate delivery mechanisms easier to test without duplicating tool behavior.

tour.title: Vault Resolution Safety
tour.description: Configuration converts environment-supplied named vaults into controlled targets and provides path-resolution helpers for every filesystem operation. Safety helpers then describe mutation risk, read-only refusal, untrusted content, and byte-delta protections so clients can make informed calls.

tour.title: Tool Surface Tiers
tour.description: The registry is the server's single exposure point: it combines handlers, dynamic vault schemas, filtering, and safety annotations. Its categories distinguish 75 Node-only filesystem tools, one always-listed but explicitly invoked app-contact tool, and 28 CLI-only tools whose runtime API access fails clearly when Obsidian is unavailable.

tour.title: Exact Graph Consent
tour.description: Graph analysis defaults to an exact prepared snapshot, but it cannot open Obsidian or quietly substitute a filesystem result. The separate open-and-prepare route validates one configured registered vault identity, then stores a cloned session-only snapshot with serialized preparation and invalidation behavior before ranking can proceed.

tour.title: Graph Authority Truth
tour.description: Provider selection keeps runtime-derived and filesystem-derived graph data distinct, exposing what authority actually built a returned graph. The provider-state tests protect the accompanying recovery, fallback-reason, cache, and capability metadata contracts, so an approximation is never presented as exact Obsidian state.

tour.title: Cross-Vault URI Overlay
tour.description: Cross-vault relationships are declared through validated obsidian://open URIs rather than native same-vault wikilinks. URI parsing, diagnostics, and graph construction produce a typed read-only overlay of only eligible declarations; it never rewrites notes or enters a vault's BaseGraph, ranking, or retrieval ordering.

tour.title: Retrieval Evaluation
tour.description: Semantic tools manage optional embedding-backed retrieval while preserving honest indexing and availability information. The metrics module and evaluation guide turn ranked results into measurable precision, recall, DCG, and reciprocal-rank evidence instead of treating search quality as a subjective claim.

tour.title: AI Team Workflow
tour.description: Repository instructions establish evidence ordering, scoped ownership, implementation boundaries, and verification expectations for collaborators. The operating model explains how research, implementation, tests, and independent review fit together while leaving product and release decisions with the founder.

tour.title: Behavioral Test Gates
tour.description: The built-output test suites verify tool registration parity, dynamic schemas, and disabled-tool filtering alongside the exact-graph consent boundary and both transports. These are behavior-level checks: they confirm the safety and capability promises introduced in earlier steps rather than merely compiling the source.

tour.title: Package and CI
tour.description: The package manifest defines the npm product, scripts, dependencies, and packaging inputs. Before release, isolated package verification exercises the packed artifact and its native binding; CI repeats clean installs, builds, coverage tests, package checks, and coverage upload on Node 20 and 22.
tour.languageLesson: CI workflows make the build matrix explicit: each job starts from a clean environment, so a passing local checkout is not mistaken for a reproducible package.
